 Single transition metal atom embedded
Published on 28 June 2021. Downloaded by The University of Tokyo on 11/26/2025 10:17:30 AM.

 Cite this: Nanoscale, 2021, 13, 12885
 antimonene monolayers as eﬃcient trifunctional
 electrocatalysts for the HER, OER and ORR:
 a density functional theory study†
 Song Lu,a Huong Lan Huynh,a Fengliu Lou,b Kun Guo *c and Zhixin Yu *a

 Highly eﬃcient, stable and cost-eﬀective electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER),
 oxygen evolution reaction (OER), and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) have been pursued for several
 decades. Herein, by employing density functional theory (DFT), a wide range of transition metal (TM = Sc,
 Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Cd, Ir, Pt and Au) atoms anchored on antimonene (Sb
 monolayer) with a single Sb vacancy as single-atom catalysts (SACs) were investigated for their HER, OER
 and ORR performance. The results indicate that the defective Sb monolayer can be stable. Some TM@Sb
 monolayers show excellent stability and good electrical conductivity, beneﬁcial for electron transfer
 during electrocatalytic reactions. The Ir@ and Pt@Sb monolayers exhibit excellent HER performance, both
 with about −0.01 eV of ΔG*H. The d band centre of the TM@Sb monolayer can be used to describe the
 binding strength between substrates and intermediates directly. The best OER electrocatalyst is the Pt@Sb
 monolayer, which shows an overpotential (ηOER) of 0.48 V. In contrast, the best ORR electrocatalyst is the
 Ag@Sb monolayer with an ηORR of 0.50 V, followed by Pd@, Rh@, Cd@ and Pt@Sb monolayers. Compared
 Received 10th April 2021, with pristine antimonene, only the noble metal atom could improve its OER and ORR performance eﬀec-
 Accepted 27th June 2021
 tively, and the Pt@Sb monolayer can be a trifunctional electrocatalyst for the HER/OER/ORR. Therefore,
 DOI: 10.1039/d1nr02235k our calculations highlight a new type of SAC based on antimonene, which can be useful for energy con-
 rsc.li/nanoscale version and storage.

 Ag@Sb monolayer is evaluated at the PBE+U level. The result
 is the same as the Ir@ and Pt @Sb monolayer, showing a very

 suggesting TM sites are indeed the active sites. No imaginary

 the Ag@Sb monolayer (Fig. S10a†). AIMD simulation for

 = −2.57, ΔGc = −0.74 and ΔGd = −0.73 eV, respectively, while it
 is −1.14, −2.12, −1.01 and −0.65 eV for the Pd@Sb monolayer.

 Nanoscale Paper

 as the active sites for the HER, OER and ORR have been inves-
 tigated. We demonstrated that almost all TM@Sb monolayers
 could present good stability to form SACs. Meanwhile, some of
 the SACs also show good electrical conductivity. For the HER,
 the Ir@, Pt@, Ni@, and Cu@Sb monolayers show a small
 value of ΔG*H (−0.009, −0.010, 0.059 and 0.193 eV, respect-
 ively). In terms of OER performance, the Pt@Sb monolayer
 shows the smallest ηOER of 0.48 V, which is smaller than the
 state-of-the-art catalyst IrO2 (0.56 V). The binding strength of
Published on 28 June 2021. Downloaded by The University of Tokyo on 11/26/2025 10:17:30 AM.

 substrates and intermediates displays a close correlation with
 the d band center of TM atoms. For the ORR performance of
 antimonene based SACs, the overpotential ηORR of the Ag@Sb
 monolayer is the smallest at only 0.50 V, followed by Pd@,
 Rh@, Cd@ and Pt@Sb monolayers (0.58 V, 0.60 V, 0.62 V and
 0.71 V, respectively). The noble metal atoms can improve the
 OER and ORR performances of antimonene better than other
 TM atoms. It could be suggested that the Pt@Sb monolayer
 Fig. 7 (a) Scaling relations between ΔG*OH and ΔG*OOH for TM@Sb
 monolayers; (b) scaling relations between the ΔG*OH and ΔG*O for can be a trifunctional electrocatalyst for HER, OER and ORR
 TM@Sb monolayers. reactions. Our studies predicate a new type of catalyst with a
 single TM atom anchored on antimonene, which could be
 applied in water splitting, metal–air batteries and fuel cells.

 S. Lu, K. Guo and Z. Yu designed the research. S. Lu performed
 DFT and AIMD simulations. All authors collaboratively ana-
 lyzed the data. S. Lu and Z. Yu contributed to the interpret-
 ation of the results. All authors wrote the paper and prepared
 revisions.
